title.value: Dissecting the phenotypic heterogeneity in sensory features in autism spectrum disorder: a factor mixture modelling approach
title.justification: The title of the paper clearly states the focus on the phenotypic heterogeneity in sensory features in autism spectrum disorder using a factor mixture modelling approach.
title.quote: Dissecting the phenotypic heterogeneity in sensory features in autism spectrum disorder: a factor mixture modelling approach

analysis.description: This paper applies factor mixture modelling (FMM) to test a multidimensional factor model of sensory processing in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The research aims to identify homogeneous sensory subgroups in ASD, examining how these subgroups differ intrinsically in severity along continuous factor scores. It also investigates the relationships between sensory subgroups and various clinical variables such as age, IQ, and different behavioral symptoms. This study uses data from 332 individuals with ASD and focuses on improving the understanding of the heterogeneity of sensory features in ASD.

type.justification: The paper involves statistical and methodological approaches to investigating heterogeneity in sensory features of ASD in a sample of 332 individuals, which indicates empirical research.
type.quote: Methods: Three hundred thirty-two children and adults with ASD between the ages of 6 and 30 years with IQs varying between 40 and 148 were included.

name.justification: The primary focus of the study is on sensory features in individuals with autism spectrum disorder, which is clearly stated in the title and throughout the paper.

name.justification: The study specifically investigates the sensory features in ASD, aiming to understand their heterogeneity and relevance to other clinical symptoms.
name.quote: Background: Heterogeneity in the phenotypic presentation of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is apparent in the profile and the severity of sensory features.

name.justification: The research utilizes factor mixture modelling to investigate the multidimensional structure of sensory features in ASD.
name.quote: Factor mixture modelling (FMM [39]) is a flexible hybrid model that combines LCA and FA approaches by simultaneously modelling the underlying structure to be both categorical and dimensional.

is_contributed.justification: FMM is a known technique in statistical modelling and is not a new contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: Factor mixture modelling (FMM [39]) is a flexible hybrid model...

is_executed.justification: The study employs FMM to analyze the sensory features data from 332 individuals with ASD.
is_executed.quote: the ‘three-subgroup/seven-factor’ FMM provided the best fit to the data and was superior to all other models...

is_compared.justification: FMM was compared to other models like LCA and CFA in terms of fit to the data.
is_compared.quote: A direct comparison of all competing models demonstrated that the ‘three-subgroup/seven-factor’ FMM provided the best fit to the data and was superior to all other models (CFA, LCA and FMM) based on all goodness-of-fit criteria...
